chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever relieves a believer (of distress), Allah will relieve his heart on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.فَرَّجَ: to relieve, to remove distress or hardship

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for relieving a believer's distress?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) highlights the profound spiritual reciprocity of relieving a believer's distress, promising divine ease for the heart on the Day of Judgment. In Shia tradition, this act is viewed as a means of purifying the soul and securing Allah's mercy, reflecting the interconnectedness of the Ummah's spiritual well-being. It underscores the practical application of faith through active compassion and support for fellow believers.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who relieves (a suffering) from a Momin, Allahazwj would Relieve from his heart on the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 4. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever relieves a believer from suffering, Allah will provide relief for his (helper’s) heart on the Day of Judgment.”
